subject: Clarify how Redwood treats request/response artifacts and deletion options
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: How long do you keep prompts + responses by default?

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question from our security review: when a user sends a prompt to your hosted API, what is retained by default? Specifically:
- Do you persist raw request text (prompts) and full model outputs?
- If so, what is the default retention period for those logs in the hosted product?
- Can we opt to prevent storage of prompts or outputs at ingest time?
- What are the deletion options if we need to purge historical data for a subset of our tenant IDs?

We need concise answers for our security questionnaire and any links to procedural docs or evidence would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Sarah
Security Program Manager
Acme Health

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: How long do you keep prompts + responses by default?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list of asks. High-level answers up front, then I'll loop in Kim/Marissa for specifics and evidence links:

1) Short answer: by default our hosted API stores request/response artifacts (prompts and generated outputs) for 45 days for operational telemetry and quality monitoring.
2) Prompts vs derivatives: we treat raw prompt text and model outputs as "stored artifacts" by default. Certain derivatives (e.g., embeddings or aggregated usage counters) may be surfaced separately.
3) Opt-out: you can request prompt/output non-retention via account settings or via a tenant-level flag for Dedicated/Private; for hosted customers we can enable a non-retention setting at the tenancy level subject to contract.
4) Deletion: we support on-demand deletion for specific tenant IDs and can run a scoped purge; permanent deletion is reflected in our audit log and we can provide a report.

Attaching a short CSV that summarizes default retention categories and the typical purge path. Kim — can you confirm the default retention windows and whether the 45-day default applies uniformly to interactive requests, streaming, and embeddings? Marissa — can you add the support ticket link and any evidence (S3 object lifecycle snapshots) we can provide to Acme?

Next step: Kim to confirm retention windows and Marissa to propose evidence artifacts. I'll stay on thread to coordinate.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_retention_summary_2028-07.csv

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sarah@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: How long do you keep prompts + responses by default?

Thanks Vanessa — confirming details for the record. I'll keep this terse so you can paste into Acme's questionnaire: 

- Default retention period (hosted): 45 days for full request/response artifacts (this includes prompt text and the model-generated tokens).
- Scope: applies to synchronous API calls (text generation/chat), streaming sessions (buffered segments are retained as assembled artifacts), and embeddings (raw input and resulting vectors are retained under the same policy unless otherwise configured).
- Purpose: retention is used for debugging, quality monitoring, rate-limit abuse detection, and to train internal pipeline heuristics. We do not train user-facing model weights with hosted customer prompt data unless a separate data-sharing agreement is in place.
- Opt-out configuration: for hosted customers we can enable a tenant-level "non-storage" flag that prevents persistent storage of request/response artifacts; note this disables some debugging/rollback features and will remove access to certain console-level analytics. For Dedicated and Private customers, retention defaults are controlled by the customer's deployment config and can be set to shorter windows or zero retention.
- On-demand purge: we support scoped deletion by tenant_id, date range, and/or artifact type (prompts / outputs / embeddings). Purge actions are executed via an internal job; completion is recorded in our audit logs and we provide a deletion report. Typical purge SLA: 72 hours for non-exempt data.
- Exceptions: system logs required for billing and core security telemetry may be retained longer (up to 365 days) but those logs are hashed/aggregated and do not contain raw prompt/output text.

I can attach the audit log sample and the internal runbook for scoped purges. One operational note: if Acme requests both deletion and a residency constraint (e.g., EU-only storage), we recommend performing residency changes first and then running the purge to ensure any cross-region copies are handled according to the new policy.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-request-forms.pdf

Hi Sarah — following up with the operational links and evidence you asked for.

Quick checklist and what we can deliver today:
- Summary CSV (attached) that Vanessa included — outlines default windows and who to contact for non-retention.
- Support ticket created: RED-81234 (shows the scoped purge workflow and expected SLA). You can view it here: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/RED-81234
- Evidence options we can provide:
  * Redacted audit log sample showing a completed tenant-level purge (we redact tenant IDs in shared samples).
  * Lifecycle policy snapshots for hosted buckets showing the 45-day TTL rules.
  * If you need a written attestation, we can generate a short statement for your compliance folder.

If Acme wants a tenant-level non-retention flag enabled, we need an approval signature and an IP allowlist for any support-assisted troubleshooting sessions. I attached the standard request form — fill and return and I will route it to our Privacy Ops team.

Let me know which of the evidence items you want first and whether you want us to enable a non-retention flag for your account. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
